about: Real facts about trucks, one shown at a time on the loading screens (src/game/loader.js). Keep each to one or two short sentences, true, and about trucks or driving them. They are shuffled and never repeat in a row.
facts: The BelAZ 75710 is the biggest dump truck ever built. It can carry about 450 tonnes in a single load.
Australian road trains pull three or four trailers and can stretch past 50 metres.
On US interstates a loaded semi-truck can weigh up to 80,000 lb, about 36 tonnes.
The top engine in a Volvo FH16 makes 3,550 Nm of torque, around ten times a family car's.
The tires on the biggest mining trucks stand about 4 metres tall and weigh over 5 tonnes each.
Mud tires have wide gaps between their lugs, so the mud flings out as they spin instead of packing in.
Letting air out of the tires widens their footprint, which helps a heavy truck float over mud, sand and snow.
Military trucks like the Ural-4320 can change their tire pressure while driving, to cross soft ground.
A locked differential turns both wheels on an axle together, so one spinning wheel cannot waste all the power.
A diesel's engine brake slows a heavy truck on long hills without wearing out its wheel brakes.
Truck air brakes are held off by air pressure. If the air is lost, strong springs put the brakes on by themselves.
Trucks carry around 70% of all freight, by weight, in the United States.
Rotator tow trucks have a crane that turns all the way around, so they can lift a wreck from any side.
A winch pulls hardest on its last few wraps of cable, closest to the drum.
Corduroy roads, logs laid side by side across soft ground, have been used to cross swamps for centuries.
Ice road truckers in northern Canada drive slowly over frozen lakes, so the wave they push under the ice cannot crack it.
